investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, causing each pod to remain stuck unscheduled for ~145–147 seconds before the eval timed out and returned no evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt fails immediately at the scheduler, preventing the eval runner from reaching the agent creation, VM-ID assignment, or state-polling stages. As a result, none of the required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is ever produced, and all three remote-agent checks fail. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval at this time.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, causing each pod to remain stuck unscheduled for ~145–147 seconds before the eval timed out and returned no evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt fails immediately at the scheduler, preventing the eval runner from reaching the agent creation, VM-ID assignment, or state-polling stages. As a result, none of the required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is ever produced, and all three remote-agent checks fail. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets only nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label, but 4 of 6 nodes do not carry that label or taint, reducing the schedulable pool to 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or a node label was removed, effective capacity is further constrained.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata-capable nodes may have an insufficient total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota for the concurrent eval load (3 checks × 1 pod each submitted in rapid succession), causing all three to compete for the same exhausted resource.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity and Node Affinity Mismatch Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-08T09:12–09:17Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval runner received no response evidence whatsoever — all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing and the expected assertion (message containsIgnoreCase "hello from aura") could not be evaluated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm runtime in production-api has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With 0 of 6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~145–147 seconds before the eval timed out. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-detected infrastructure failure.

All three sibling checks failed with the same message within minutes of each other, confirming this is not a single-pod anomaly.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, meaning only 2 nodes are eligible. If those 2 nodes recently lost capacity (e.g., due to other workloads, node scaling events, or VM quota changes), the effective schedulable pool dropped to zero.

TERTIARY — Cluster autoscaler not provisioning new kata-capable nodes in time: if autoscaling is configured, it may not have added new kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes before the eval's ~150s timeout window expired.

LOWER — Eval infrastructure issue causing incorrect pod spec (wrong node selector or resource request): less likely given that all three sibling checks produced the same scheduling error with consistent timing, suggesting the pod spec is consistent and the cluster is the constraint.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the affinity-matching nodes at the time of the failure, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a pod spec or API misconfiguration would become more likely.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds and produces all 5 required evidence fields, the issue was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike or a leaked pod that was cleaned up) rather than a sustained capacity shortage.

If the node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec was recently changed to exclude previously eligible nodes, and that change explains why only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible, then a configuration drift rather than raw capacity exhaustion would be the primary cause.

If other non-remote-agent workloads (not eval pods) are shown to have consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the cause would be external workload pressure rather than an eval or remote-agent-specific issue.

If the local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) passed during the same run window, that would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote/kata peer-pod scheduling path and not a broader API or authentication failure.

Add a cluster node affinity/selector validation eval that confirms at least N nodes match the remote agent pod's scheduling constraints, alerting early if the eligible node pool drops below a safe threshold.
Add a pod scheduling latency eval that measures time-to-scheduled for remote agent pods and warns before the full eval timeout is reached, enabling faster triage of scheduling vs. runtime failures.

Consider adding a sibling check for leaked or stuck remote agent pods (pods in Pending/Unschedulable state for more than a configurable threshold) to detect capacity leaks from prior eval runs before they exhaust the VM slot pool.
